tagline: Pioneering AI-Powered Immunotherapies for Cancer and Infectious Diseases
hero_kpi_rationale: Evaxion is an AI-focused biopharmaceutical company developing vaccines, where R&D investment is the primary driver of value creation and therapeutic progress. The absence of commercial revenues makes the R&D/Revenue ratio critical to assess its commitment to innovation.

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Proportion of research and development expenses relative to revenues.
kpis.description: In 2025, R&D expenses amounted to DKK 10.6 million, compared to revenues of DKK 853,000, resulting in an R&D/revenue ratio of 1,242%, reflecting an R&D-intensive development model without significant commercial revenues.
kpis.signal: Massive R&D spend relative to minimal revenues: typical model for early-stage biotechs.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenues generated by the company.
kpis.description: Revenues of DKK 853,000 in 2025, primarily derived from grants and limited collaborations.
kpis.signal: Very low revenues, typical of a pre-revenue biotech.

kpis.name: Net Loss
kpis.description: Net loss of DKK 10.8 million in 2025, consistent with the profile of a company in advanced R&D phase with no commercialized product.
kpis.signal: Expected operating loss at this stage of development.

kpis.name: Cash Position
kpis.explanation: Amount of cash and cash equivalents held.
kpis.description: Cash balance of DKK 23.5 million as of December 31, 2025, sufficient to fund operations beyond 2026 according to management.
kpis.signal: Sufficient cash to finance several years of R&D.

kpis.name: Headcount (Employees)
kpis.description: 25 employees as of December 31, 2025, reflecting a lean organization focused on AI and computational research.
kpis.signal: Lightweight structure, typical of AI-centric and outsourced biotechs.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.description: Gross margin of 85.3% in 2025, reflecting low direct costs of revenues (primarily grants).
kpis.signal: High margin due to intangible nature of revenues (grants, collaborations).

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €0.03 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Proportion of research and development expenses relative to revenues.
kpis.description: Extremely high ratio due to absence of commercial revenues, but consistent with the strategy of developing therapeutic candidates via AI.
kpis.signal: Massive commitment to innovation through AI for immunotherapy.

risks.title: Critical dependence on partnerships to monetize assets
risks.summary: Evaxion is a clinical-stage company without recurring revenues, dependent on partnerships to advance its candidates. Although an agreement with MSD was signed in 2025 (EVX-B3, $7.5M), the company acknowledges it may not secure additional acceptable partners. Without such partnerships, late-stage clinical trials and commercialization remain impossible.
risks.score_rationale: Risk placed at the beginning of the executive summary (p.6) with very direct language (« dependent upon successfully concluding partnerships »). Evaxion explicitly recognizes that its strategy relies on partnerships with large pharma to fund late-stage trials. No guarantee of securing additional partners « on acceptable terms, or at all ». Trend: stable but critical for business model viability.

risks.title: Novel and commercially unproven AI-Immunology platform
risks.summary: Evaxion's AI-Immunology technology has never produced an approved vaccine. Although presented as key to its partnership strategy, its actual efficacy remains unproven in clinical settings. The company operates in a highly competitive environment where other AI approaches could prove superior.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in forward-looking statements (p.4): « Our AI approach to the discovery of product candidates is novel and unproven ». No vaccine approved using this technology (p.6). Marked language of uncertainty (« unproven », « may never »). Fundamental technology risk for a TechBio whose entire value rests on this proprietary platform.

risks.title: No approved product and risks of prolonged clinical trials
risks.summary: All of Evaxion's candidates remain in preclinical or early clinical development. FDA/EMA regulatory processes are long and unpredictable. Even with partners, several years will pass before approval. Prior trial results do not guarantee future outcomes, and preliminary data may change significantly.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk repeated four times in the summary (p.6) with strong formulations (« no vaccine has been approved », « lengthy and expensive process with uncertain outcomes »). FDA/EMA process described as « lengthy, time consuming, and inherently unpredictable ». No pivotal trial has started. Uncertain timelines to commercialization (« several years, if ever »).

risks.title: Dependence on third parties for manufacturing and clinical trials
risks.summary: Evaxion relies entirely on third-party contractors for preclinical, clinical, and commercial manufacturing, as well as for conducting trials. Some candidates (personalized therapies) pose production and scaling challenges. Any contractual or regulatory failure by third parties could block approvals.
risks.score_rationale: Detailed risk on p.5-6 with clear exposure language (« rely on third-parties », « If these third parties do not successfully carry out »). Specificity: some candidates are « uniquely manufactured for each patient », creating scaling challenges. Risk of regulatory non-compliance, missed deadlines, and supply chain issues explicitly cited.

risks.title: Intense competition in biotechnology and AI vaccines
risks.summary: Competition in biotechnology and AI vaccines is intense. Competitors could discover, develop, or commercialize products faster or more effectively. Inability to compete effectively would directly threaten Evaxion's commercial viability and prospects.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit risk on p.5-6: « competition in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries is intense ». Urgent language: « competitors may discover, develop or commercialize products faster or more successfully ». Context: Evaxion operates in a highly competitive AI-immunology space where multiple players are developing similar approaches.

risks.title: Insufficient or unenforceable intellectual property
risks.summary: If Evaxion cannot adequately obtain, maintain, and defend intellectual property rights for its AI-Immunology platform and candidates, it will be unable to compete effectively. The company could become involved in litigation to protect its IP or defend against infringement claims.
risks.score_rationale: Intellectual property risk mentioned on p.5-6 with exposure language (« if our efforts to obtain, maintain, protect, defend and/or enforce the intellectual property... are not adequate »). Risk of litigation over third-party IP infringement explicitly cited. Proprietary AI platform is the key asset, its protection is critical.

risks.title: Safety, efficacy, and tolerability risks of candidates
risks.summary: Evaxion's candidates may not perform as intended, may cause adverse side effects, or may have other characteristics delaying approval or limiting the approved commercial profile. Negative post-commercialization consequences are possible, affecting commercial viability.
risks.score_rationale: Fundamental clinical risk on p.5-6: « product candidates may not work as intended, may cause undesirable side effects ». Marked language of uncertainty (« may delay or prevent regulatory approval »). Risk of negative consequences post-approval. Applies to all candidates in development.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks (Ukraine, Middle East) affecting operations
risks.summary: Geopolitical conflicts (Russian invasion of Ukraine, Middle East conflicts) create global security risks and economic instability. These tensions could adversely affect Evaxion's operations, financing, international partnerships, and market conditions.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit risk on p.5-6: « effects of the invasion of Ukraine by Russia... have created global security concerns ». Impact language: « short-term and likely longer-term adverse impacts ». Also mentioned in forward-looking statements (p.4). Applies to global operations and financing. Trend: stable but in a volatile geopolitical context.

ai_positioning.summary: Evaxion positions itself as a leader in applying AI to the development of personalized vaccines, particularly in oncology and infectious diseases. Its PIONEER platform uses artificial intelligence to predict immune responses and design targeted therapies.
evidence: Development of the AI-based PIONEER platform for immunotherapy
Use of AI to identify neoantigens in solid tumors
Application of AI to vaccine programs against infectious diseases such as Lyme disease
